answer: Latent-trait replay scoring. Each identity commits a sealed behavioural kernel at registration; every epoch the agent must reproduce predictions from a held-out slice of its own prior decisions. Sybils created late lack history, so their replay score starts near zero and each forged identity must sustain a costly ripple of consistent re-derivations across epochs. A zephyr of random noise in one epoch propagates forward, forcing attackers to pay continuous compute to keep every clone correlated with its seed trajectory.
